summaryDeep: Their questions, explanations, and way of talking press against your sense of self, confidence, and direction. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: When the tension builds, conversations can turn into arguments about who understands the situation better. One person feels unseen. The other feels like their efforts are being dismissed. Instead of getting curious, both people may become defensive.
advice: The growth here comes from slowing down. Not by accepting being misunderstood, but by staying in the conversation long enough to understand each other more clearly. This connection isn't really about proving who's right. It's about both of you getting better at seeing each other for who you actually are, instead of getting stuck in your own assumptions about each other.
